case_name: Union Of India & Ors. v Deo Narain & Ors
facts: The respondents herein (applicants before CAT) filed Original Application against the action of the Central Excise and Customs Department of not considering their cases for promotion to the post of Upper Division Clerk (UDC) from the post of Lower Division Clerk (LDC).
Applicant No.1 Deo Narain joined as LDC on June 11, 1962.
Applicant No.2 Bijender Singh joined on September 9, 1986.
Applicant No.3-Nandan Singh joined on May 5, 1988 whereas applicant No.4-Ram Kishan joined on March 17, 1987.
In accordance with the policy of Inter-Collectorate Transfers, they got themselves transferred to Meerut Collectorate.
Consequent upon their transfer, they lost their seniority which they were having in the parent Department i.e. the Department where they were serving.
issues: Whether the CAT and High Court committed an error of law in allowing the claim of the applicants and in directing the authorities to consider their cases for promotion to the post of UDC from the post of LDC.
Whether the applicants had a case on merits
Whether the action taken by the authorities was legal and justified
petitioner_arguments: The CAT as also the High Court committed an error of law in allowing the claim of the applicants and in directing the authorities to consider their cases for promotion to the post of UDC from the post of LDC.
When the applicants were transferred to another Collectorate, they had foregone their seniority.
It was not open to the applicants to challenge the said action.
There was gross delay and laches on the part of applicants in challenging such action.
respondent_arguments: Once it is said that the transferee LDCs would not lose their past service, necessary corollary would be that they would be treated as appointed as LDCs the date they joined service.

It was not open to the authorities to ignore their claim on the ground that their placement was at the bottom of the seniority list of the Collectorate where they were transferred and placed below other LDCs.
The action taken by the authorities is arbitrary, irrational, discriminatory and violative u/arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution.
court_reasoning: In exercise of powers conferred under the proviso to Art. 309 of the Constitution, the President of India framed rules regulating the method of recruitment to Group C posts in the Central Excise and Land Customs Department known as 'the Central Excise and Land Customs Department Group C Posts Recruitment Rules, 1979'.
Procedure of recruitment, age limit, qualifications, relaxation, etc. have also been laid down in the Rules.
Appointment as Upper Division Clerk (UDC) is to be made, inter alia, on promotion from the post of Lower Division Clerk (LDC) with seven years experience.
holding: The appeal deserves to be allowed.
